The Abia State Government has announced the immediate dissolution of the management structure and technical crew of Enyimba International Football Club, Aba. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the state Commissioner for Information, Okey Kanu, said the decision was “in a decisive move to address the club’s recent disappointing performances and identified administrative and structural challenges”. The statement said the decision “underscores the government’s resolve to undertake a comprehensive restructuring of the two-time CAF Champions League winners, restore the club’s competitive identity and reposition it for sustainable success in Nigerian and continental football”. It further stated, “Following a review of the club’s current state of affairs, the government has concluded that far-reaching interventions are necessary to address the underlying issues affecting its performance, administration and overall operations. “Consequently, the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development has been mandated to lead the restructuring process, undertake a comprehensive assessment of the club’s management framework and implement appropriate administrative, technical, operational and institutional reforms aimed at restoring stability, accountability and competitiveness. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “The dissolution takes immediate effect”. The government directed all affected management and technical personnel, as well as anyone in possession of Enyimba International FC’s assets, properties, official documents, equipment and other institutional materials, “to ensure an orderly and formal handover of all such items to the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development”. According to the statement, the ministry will communicate further details regarding the handover arrangements and subsequent administrative procedures. The Abia State Government acknowledged Enyimba’s historic place in Nigerian and African football as one of the country’s most successful and decorated football institutions, noting that “the club’s legacy remains an important sporting heritage of Abia State, and the government is determined to safeguard that legacy while laying the foundation for a more professionally managed and competitive future”. The government also reassured Enyimba supporters, players, stakeholders and the general public that the intervention was aimed at securing the club’s long-term interests, strengthening its institutional capacity and restoring the pride, identity and competitive standards associated with the Enyimba name.
